cards.hypothesis: Subject-specific baseline heart rate variability influences conformal prediction coverage stability.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Higher baseline HRV leads to larger prediction errors, causing conformal intervals to be too narrow and resulting in under-coverage.
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage fluctuations are due to random noise in the conformal algorithm rather than subject traits.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage variability will be uncorrelated with baseline HRV across subjects.
cards.distinguishing_test: If coverage correlates negatively with baseline HRV after controlling for age and medication, the mechanism is supported; if no correlation, the rival is supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Prior work shows moderate association between HRV and prediction error in physiological signals.
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with higher baseline HRV will exhibit lower coverage than those with lower HRV.
cards.failure_condition: No significant difference in coverage between high and low HRV groups.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed-effects model with coverage as outcome, baseline_HRV as fixed effect, subject as random effect, controlling for age and medication.
cards.falsification_test: Pharmacologically reduce HRV (e.g., via beta-blocker) and test whether coverage moves toward the nominal level; failure to change falsifies the mechanism.

cards.hypothesis: Sensor drift induces non-stationary noise that breaks conformal prediction's exchangeability assumption.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Gradual baseline shift in sensor output changes signal mean, altering error distribution and causing miscalibrated intervals.
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage failure stems from temporal autocorrelation violating exchangeability, not sensor drift.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage loss will be similar across sensors regardless of measured drift magnitude.
cards.distinguishing_test: If coverage deficit correlates with sensor drift after adjusting for temperature and humidity, the mechanism is supported; otherwise the rival is supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Sensor drift can produce substantial bias in physiological measurements, leading to large coverage errors.
cards.testable_prediction: Segments with higher sensor drift will show lower coverage.
cards.failure_condition: No association between sensor drift magnitude and coverage.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Partial correlation between sensor drift magnitude and coverage deficit, controlling for temperature and humidity.
cards.falsification_test: Perform sensor recalibration mid-experiment; if coverage improves to nominal after recalibration, the mechanism is supported; if coverage does not improve, it is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Arousal-induced heteroscedasticity in physiological signals leads to conformal prediction coverage instability.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Increased arousal raises signal variance, widening prediction errors; conformal's assumption of homoscedastic error causes intervals to be too narrow during high arousal, producing under-coverage.
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability arises from model misspecification (e.g., using linear relationships) rather than arousal-driven variance changes.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deficits will be uniform across arousal levels if the model is misspecified.
cards.distinguishing_test: If coverage deficit correlates with arousal after adjusting for time of day and caffeine, the mechanism is supported; if not, the rival is supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Arousal is known to moderately affect variance of signals such as heart rate and skin conductance.
cards.testable_prediction: Higher arousal will be associated with lower coverage (under-coverage).
cards.failure_condition: No significant correlation between arousal level and coverage deficit.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Regression of coverage deficit on arousal level with random intercept for subject, controlling for time of day and caffeine intake.
cards.falsification_test: Induce a calm state via guided breathing and measure coverage; if coverage does not return to nominal, the mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Circadian phase shifts alter baseline physiological levels, causing conformal prediction coverage to vary across the day.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Changes in circadian phase shift the mean of physiological signals, leading to systematic errors in nonconformity scores and fluctuating coverage.
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage changes are due to batch effects in data processing pipelines across time, not circadian biology.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage defects will align with processing batch boundaries irrespective of circadian phase.
cards.distinguishing_test: If coverage variation aligns with circadian phase after adjusting for batch effects, the mechanism is supported; if it aligns with batch, the rival is supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Circadian effects on physiological baselines are typically modest, leading to small coverage deviations.
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage will be lowest during the biological night (high melatonin).
cards.failure_condition: No difference in coverage across circadian phase bins.
cards.statistical_test_plan: ANOVA comparing coverage across circadian phase bins, controlling for processing batch as a covariate.
cards.falsification_test: Apply a constant routine protocol to eliminate circadian variation; if coverage remains unstable, the mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Systematic labeling errors in the reference standard bias conformal prediction nonconformity scores, destabilizing coverage.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Mislabelled events (e.g., false arrhythmia annotations) produce consistently high or low nonconformity scores, shifting the empirical quantile used for interval construction and causing over- or under-coverage.
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage failure results from the algorithm's sensitivity to outliers, not from labeling errors.
cards.rival_prediction: Segments with many outliers will show coverage loss regardless of label error rate.
cards.distinguishing_test: If correcting label errors improves coverage while outlier removal does not, the mechanism is supported; if the opposite, the rival is supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Label errors can drastically shift empirical quantiles, producing large coverage deviations.
cards.testable_prediction: Segments with higher label disagreement will exhibit lower coverage.
cards.failure_condition: No relationship between label disagreement rate and coverage.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Logistic regression of coverage failure (binary) on proportion of disputed labels, adjusting for signal artifact rate.
cards.falsification_test: Obtain blind re-annotations from an expert panel; if coverage reaches nominal using the corrected labels, the mechanism is supported; if coverage does not improve, it is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Failure to stratify conformal prediction by activity type leads to heterogeneous error distributions and unstable coverage.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Different activities (e.g., walking vs resting) generate distinct signal dynamics; pooling violates exchangeability, causing activity-specific over- or under-coverage.
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability stems from insufficient calibration set size rather than activity heterogeneity.
cards.rival_prediction: Increasing the calibration set size will uniformly improve coverage across all activities.
cards.distinguishing_test: If computing conformal separately for each activity restores nominal coverage, the mechanism is supported; if coverage remains off despite stratification, the rival is supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Activity-related changes in signal statistics are moderate but sufficient to affect conformal quantiles.
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage during walking will be lower than during rest when a single conformal model is used.
cards.failure_condition: No difference in coverage between activity types.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Compute coverage per activity and test difference using a chi-square test of proportions.
cards.falsification_test: Apply activity-specific conformal calibration; if coverage becomes nominal across all activities, the mechanism is supported; if coverage remains off, it is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Temporal autocorrelation within physiological signal segments violates the exchangeability assumption of conformal prediction, leading to coverage loss.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Strong lag-1 autocorrelation creates dependence among nonconformity scores, biasing the empirical quantile low and producing intervals that are too narrow.
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage loss is due to model underfitting (e.g., overly simple predictor) rather than temporal dependence.
cards.rival_prediction: Increasing model complexity will fix coverage regardless of autocorrelation level.
cards.distinguishing_test: If decorrelating scores (e.g., via block bootstrap) restores nominal coverage, the mechanism is supported; if coverage does not improve, the rival is supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: The magnitude of the effect depends on the autocorrelation structure; it will be estimated from data by regressing coverage deficit on lag-1 autocorrelation.
cards.testable_prediction: Higher lag-1 autocorrelation will be associated with lower coverage.
cards.failure_condition: No significant association between lag-1 autocorrelation and coverage deficit.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear regression of coverage deficit on lag-1 autocorrelation, controlling for sampling rate and filter order.
cards.falsification_test: Generate surrogate data that destroys temporal dependence (phase randomization); if coverage becomes nominal, the mechanism is supported; if coverage does not change, it is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Heavy-tailed error distributions cause conformal prediction intervals to be too narrow in the tails, reducing coverage for extreme values.
cards.proposed_mechanism: High kurtosis in prediction errors leads to underestimated tail mass; conformal's empirical quantile fails to capture extreme errors, resulting in under-coverage in the distribution tails.
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage loss arises from using an inappropriate conformity score function (e.g., absolute error) rather than heavy tails.
cards.rival_prediction: Switching to a different score (e.g., squared error) will fix coverage regardless of error kurtosis.
cards.distinguishing_test: If using a robustness-oriented score (e.g., Huber loss) improves tail coverage, the mechanism is supported; if not, the rival is supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Heavy tails may affect only extreme quantiles, producing modest changes in overall coverage.
cards.testable_prediction: Segments with higher error kurtosis will show lower coverage in the 95% tails.
cards.failure_condition: No difference in tail coverage between high and low kurtosis groups.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Compare tail coverage between high vs low kurtosis groups using Welch's t-test.
cards.falsification_test: Apply a heavy-tail aware conformal method (e.g., quantile regression forests); if coverage normalizes, the mechanism is supported; if coverage remains off, it is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Subject-specific medication alters both the mean and variance of physiological signals, leading to conformal prediction coverage instability.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Medication (e.g., beta-blockers) reduces heart rate mean and variability, shifting error distribution and causing conformal intervals to be misaligned, producing either over- or under-coverage depending on direction.
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability is due to time-varying noise unrelated to medication.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage deficits will be uncorrelated with medication status after accounting for time-varying noise.
cards.distinguishing_test: If coverage differs between medicated and non-medicated subjects after controlling for age and underlying condition, the mechanism is supported; if not, the rival is supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Medications like beta-blockers are known to produce moderate changes in heart rate mean and variance.
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects taking medication will have coverage that deviates from nominal in a consistent direction (e.g., under-coverage for beta-blockers).
cards.failure_condition: No significant difference in coverage between medicated and non-medicated groups.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Two-sample t-test comparing coverage between medicated and non-medicated subjects, controlling for age and underlying condition via ANCOVA.
cards.falsification_test: Withdraw medication in a crossover design; if coverage moves toward nominal, the mechanism is supported; if coverage does not change, it is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Class imbalance in the calibration set causes conformal prediction to produce intervals with systematically incorrect coverage for the minority class.
cards.proposed_mechanism: When the calibration set under-represents a physiological state (e.g., arrhythmia), the empirical quantile used for interval width is dominated by the majority class, leading to intervals that are too narrow for the minority class and under-coverage.
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage loss for minority class stems from the predictor's poor performance on that class, not from conformal calibration.
cards.rival_prediction: Improving the predictor's accuracy on the minority class will fix coverage regardless of class imbalance.
cards.distinguishing_test: If reweighting the calibration set to balance classes restores nominal coverage for the minority class while predictor accuracy unchanged, the mechanism is supported; if coverage does not improve, the rival is supported.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Severe class imbalance can shift quantiles substantially, producing large coverage errors.
cards.testable_prediction: Segments belonging to the minority class will exhibit lower coverage than those from the majority class when using a standard conformal predictor.
cards.failure_condition: No difference in coverage between minority and majority class segments.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Logistic regression of coverage failure (binary) on class membership, adjusting for signal noise level and feature distribution shift.
cards.falsification_test: Apply class-weighted conformal prediction (e.g., weighted quantiles); if coverage for minority class reaches nominal, the mechanism is supported; if coverage remains low, it is falsified.
